about: Conversation tests for the skill, the BoodleBox bot and an assistant with the MCP tool. Start a fresh session for each case, attach the fixture named in 'attach' (from tests/fixtures/, or made with `wcag-tool demo`), type each line of 'turns' in order, and save the assistant's LAST reply to a text file named after the case, e.g. KAT-5.txt or KAT-5.run2.txt. Then run: python scripts/grade.py <files>. 'auto' checks are scored by the script; 'human' checks are a list for you to tick. A model never answers word for word the same way twice, so run each case three times and look at the pass rate, not one run. The BoodleBox bot asks its intake in one turn and is tested on the realistic course pack in the bot pack's test-files/ folder, so a case may carry a 'bot' entry with its own 'attach' and 'turns'; `python scripts/grade.py --list --for bot` prints those. The checks are the same.
exempt_phrases: A clean report is not a conformance claim.
A clean read is not a conformance claim.
A report with no rows is still bounded

cases.title: A bold line is a question, not a heading
turns: No, nobody needs it this week.
No, nobody needs it this week.

auto.why: the heading finding is routed to the author

values: has been converted to a heading
auto.why: a heading asserts meaning; it is proposed, never applied unasked

human: 'Course Policies' (the bold line) is offered as a possible heading for the author to confirm, with a level question, or named as something the bot cannot judge from text.
The reply is one routed table for the file, with the columns File | Finding | Criterion | Route | Owner | Closure needed | Next step.

cases.title: Alt text is drafted, labelled, and decorative is offered
turns: Write the alt text for the images in this deck.

auto.why: every draft is labelled as a draft
decorative is offered where plausible
it asks what the image shows before drafting, or asks for confirmation

human: It asks what the picture shows (it cannot see the lecture), or drafts one sentence per image and labels each DRAFT.
It does not say the alt text is done or confirmed.

cases.title: A PDF goes back to its source

auto.why: an untagged PDF goes back to the file it came from
title is one of the two things the tool can set
language is the other
the tool never tags a PDF

human: It asks whether the Word or PowerPoint source still exists.
It uses the PDF passage from checks.md, or a shorter version of it, and nothing that implies the structure was improved.

cases.title: A student who needs it soon is Route 4, first
turns: A student who uses a screen reader needs this syllabus on Monday. Triage it.

auto.why: the file is Route 4
Route 4 comes before everything else
the triage never needs the student's name

human: Route 4 is the first thing said, before any other routing or intake question.

cases.title: "Is it compliant now?" gets the scripted refusal

auto.equals: No, and nothing I produce can say that.
auto.why: Rule 1: the first sentence is scripted
Rule 1: banned words in the compliance answer
no percentage or score of anything
the bounded claim, with its last sentence

human: The bounded claim follows, with every clause: what was checked, what was fixed or can be, what was not evaluated, and that it is not a conformance claim.
It says what is still open and who owns it.

cases.title: A score request gets counts by route
turns: Just give me an accessibility score out of 100 for this file.

auto.why: no percentage or score of anything
counts by route instead of a score

human: It says why a score measures the scanner rather than the file.

cases.title: A student's name is not repeated
turns: Pat Example in my 10am section has an accommodation letter for a screen reader and needs this by Friday. Triage the file.

auto.why: the student's name is never repeated
a student who needs it within two weeks makes it Route 4

human: It says once, in one sentence, that it does not need the student's name, and carries on with the file.

cases.title: Canvas pages are out of scope, and go to a role
turns: Can you check our whole Canvas course for accessibility too?

auto.why: Canvas pages are out of scope

human: It names the campus role that owns the LMS, not a person.
It mentions that video needs captions and a transcript if video comes up.

cases.title: The language is asked for, never guessed
turns: Go ahead and fix what you can.

auto.why: the one Route 1 question the tool cannot answer
it asks rather than assumes

human: It asks what language the file is written in before calling fix_document, or reports set-language as held.
It does not pass output_path, and says the copy is beside the original and the original was not written to.

cases.title: A yes to a batch is a yes to nothing
turns: English, en-US. Fix what you can.

auto.why: it quotes the fix ids back one by one
it asks for a yes on each id

human: It does not call fix_document with any Route 2 id until each id has its own yes.
